system.accessHelpText:
There are three ways in – depending on who or what needs access.
Setup password – for you. Whoever wants to change layouts, sources or these settings signs in with it; the sign-in lasts 30 days in this browser. The core stores only a check value of the password, never the password itself.
Pairing – for displays. A display without access shows a six-digit code. Its request appears here under “Pair devices”: compare the code, give it a name and a level, allow it. The token travels to the display by itself; nobody has to type it.
Token – for programs without a screen, such as home-automation rules that raise a message. A token is created here, shown once, and sent by the program in the header “Authorization: Bearer …”.
The levels: “read” for a display nobody should switch from; “read and operate” for ordinary displays and for programs that raise messages; “set up” additionally for these pages. The name of an access entry is only a label – one per device or program makes sense: if a tablet is lost you remove only its entry.
Forgot the password? The sign-in page can request a setup code. The core puts it into the data folder as the file “einrichtungscode.txt” (and writes it to the log); with the code you set a new password. That way only someone who can reach the files of the installation gets back in.
Without a password and without access entries Culinola is open: on the home network everybody may do everything.

system.passwordUnset: No password has been set yet.
system.passwordSaved: Password changed. All other sign-ins have ended; this browser stays signed in.
system.passwordSavedOpen: Password set – Culinola is now protected, this browser is signed in. Displays without access show a code and appear below under “Pair devices”.
system.passwordOpenWarning: With the password Culinola is protected: all displays need access afterwards. They show a code for that, which you confirm here.
system.passwordRemoveSure: Remove the password? Without a password and without access entries Culinola is open again.
system.pairHint: A display without access shows a six-digit code and appears here. Compare the code with the one on the device, give it a name and a level, and allow it.

system.pairApproved: “{name}” is paired – the display now loads by itself.
system.tokensHint: All access entries – paired displays and those created by hand. For a program without a screen, create an entry here and enter its token there.

gate.intro: Please sign in with the setup password.

gate.resetIntro: Then prove in another way that the installation is yours: the core puts a setup code into its data folder. Whoever reads it there may set a new password. Access entries of displays and programs stay as they are.
gate.codeWhere: The code is now in the file “{file}” in Culinola’s data folder and in the core’s log. It is valid for {minutes} minutes.
gate.codeFolder: The data folder is the folder containing config.json: on a PC the “data” folder of the installation, on a NAS or Raspberry Pi the folder handed to the container as /data.
gate.mismatch: The two passwords do not match.
gate.help: How signing in and access work
gate.helpText:
Whoever sets up signs in with the setup password. The sign-in lasts 30 days in this browser and applies only to the setup pages – the display itself stays what it is unlocked as.
Displays need no password: they are paired. A display without access shows a code; after signing in you confirm it in the settings under “Pair devices”.
Programs without a screen get a token, created in the settings.
If you no longer know the password, request a setup code here. It is then in the data folder of the installation – where only someone who can reach its files anyway can read it.
